cautions: CONCEPTUAL-FIRST: the early topics (what-a-database-is, relational-databases, tables, rows, columns, data-types, keys, relationships, normalization) teach concepts with minimal SQL. The SQL topics (sql-basics through group-by, join, subqueries) may show simple real SQL as illustrative examples — keep queries short (≤8 lines), commented, and correct.
LITERACY LEVEL: no database administration, no schema design beyond intuition, no performance tuning. Indexes/transactions are their own topics — reference only elsewhere.

DEFINITIONAL DISTINCTIONS MUST BE CLEAN: row vs record vs tuple; column vs field vs attribute; table vs relation; primary key vs foreign key (uniqueness vs reference); one-to-one vs one-to-many vs many-to-many (cardinality); SELECT vs INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE (read vs write); WHERE vs GROUP BY vs ORDER BY (filter vs group vs sort); join vs subquery (combined tables vs nested query).
NO INDIVIDUALIZED ADVICE and no vendor wars: teach standard SQL concepts; mention vendor names only as examples, never as recommendations. SQL syntax shown must be standard SQL.

Distribute question answer keys EVENLY across A/B/C/D, ensuring at least one C and one D per topic. Verify keys yourself from the file, and avoid reusing identical question-stem templates across topics.
